questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Selective 1,2-reduction of cyclohex-2-en-1-one to cyclohex-2-en-1-ol in high yield is best achieved using:
questions.explanationEn: The Luche reduction ($\text{NaBH}_4 / \text{CeCl}_3\cdot 7\text{H}_2\text{O}$ in $\text{MeOH}$) uses the hard Lewis acid $\text{Ce}^{3+}$ to coordinate the carbonyl oxygen and convert $\text{BH}_4^-$ into harder alkoxyborohydride species, promoting exclusive 1,2-reduction of conjugated enones to allylic alcohols. By contrast, $\text{Li/NH}_3$, $\text{H}_2/\text{Pd-C}$, and L-Selectride perform 1,4-conjugate reduction to cyclohexanone.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Treatment of cyclohex-2-en-1-one with dimethylsulfoxonium methylide ($\text{Me}_2\text{S}^+(=\text{O})\text{CH}_2^-$, Corey-Chaykovsky reagent) in DMSO yields predominantly:
questions.explanationEn: Dimethylsulfoxonium methylide ($\text{Me}_2\text{S}^+(=\text{O})\text{CH}_2^-$) is a stabilized, softer sulfur ylide that undergoes irreversible 1,4-conjugate addition to $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ketones, followed by intramolecular displacement of $\text{DMSO}$ to yield the cyclopropyl ketone (bicyclo[4.1.0]heptan-2-one). By contrast, unstabilized dimethylsulfonium methylide ($\text{Me}_2\text{S}^+\text{CH}_2^-$) gives kinetic 1,2-addition to form the spiro-epoxide.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In the Curtius rearrangement, heating an acyl azide ($\text{RCON}_3$) in anhydrous *tert*-butanol ($t\text{-BuOH}$) produces:
questions.explanationEn: Thermal decomposition of an acyl azide ($\text{RCON}_3$) extrudes $\text{N}_2$ with concerted 1,2-migration of $\text{R}$ (with retention of stereochemistry) to generate an isocyanate ($\text{R}-\text{N}=\text{C}=\text{O}$). Trapping the isocyanate with $t\text{-BuOH}$ forms the *tert*-butyl carbamate ($\text{RNHCO}_2t\text{-Bu}$), i.e., an $N$-Boc-protected amine.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In a normal-electron-demand Diels-Alder reaction between cyclopentadiene and maleic anhydride, the kinetic preference for the *endo* adduct over the *exo* adduct is primarily attributed to:
optionsEn: Lower steric hindrance in the *endo* transition state
Stabilizing secondary orbital interactions between the $\pi^*$ orbitals of the anhydride carbonyls and the C2/C3 $p$-orbitals of the diene HOMO
Greater thermodynamic stability of the *endo* adduct
Hydrogen bonding between the anhydride oxygen and the C5 methylene group
questions.explanationEn: Although the *exo* adduct is less sterically crowded and thermodynamically more stable, the *endo* transition state places the electron-withdrawing carbonyl groups of maleic anhydride underneath the developing $\text{C}2=\text{C}3$ $\pi$-bond of cyclopentadiene. Stabilizing **secondary orbital interactions** (in-phase overlap between the diene HOMO at C2/C3 and the dienophile LUMO at the carbonyl carbons) lower the *endo* activation barrier.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In the Barton reaction, photolysis ($h\nu$) of an organic nitrite ester ($\text{RCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{ONO}$) results in remote functionalization selectively at which carbon relative to the oxygen-bearing carbon (C1)?
optionsEn: C4 ($\delta$-carbon) via a 6-membered cyclic transition state for intramolecular H-atom abstraction
C2 ($\beta$-carbon) via a 4-membered cyclic transition state
C3 ($\gamma$-carbon) via a 5-membered cyclic transition state
C5 ($\epsilon$-carbon) via a 7-membered cyclic transition state
questions.explanationEn: Photolysis of an alkyl nitrite homolytically cleaves the weak $\text{O}-\text{NO}$ bond to generate an alkoxy radical ($\text{R}'\text{O}^\bullet$) and $\text{NO}^\bullet$. The alkoxy radical selectively abstracts a hydrogen atom from the **$\delta$-carbon (C4)** through a strain-free 6-membered chair-like transition state; trapping of the resulting C4 carbon radical by $\text{NO}^\bullet$ gives a $\delta$-nitroso alcohol that tautomerizes to a $\delta$-hydroxy oxime.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following protecting-group deprotection pairs are CORRECT?
questions.explanationEn: (A) True: Silyl ethers like TBS are selectively cleaved by fluoride ion (TBAF) owing to the high $\text{Si}-\text{F}$ bond strength. (B) True: Boc groups are cleaved under acidic conditions (TFA) via *tert*-butyl cation loss and decarboxylation. (C) True: Electron-rich PMB ethers undergo selective single-electron oxidative cleavage with DDQ. (D) False: THP ethers are acetals, which are completely stable to base ($\text{NaOH}$) and are cleaved by mild acid (e.g., PPTS/EtOH). Hence, (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about 1,3-dipolar cycloadditions are CORRECT?
optionsEn: They are thermally allowed $[4\pi_s + 2\pi_s]$ ($[3+2]$) concerted cycloadditions involving $6\,\pi$ electrons
Reaction of an organic azide ($\text{R}-\text{N}_3$) with an alkyne yields a 1,2,3-triazole
Reaction of a nitrone ($\text{R}_2\text{C}=\text{N}^+(\text{R}')\text{O}^-$) with an alkene yields an isoxazolidine
They are strictly non-stereospecific with respect to the alkene dipolarophile
questions.explanationEn: (A) True: 1,3-Dipolar cycloadditions combine a $4\pi$-electron 1,3-dipole and a $2\pi$-electron dipolarophile in a concerted, thermally allowed $[4\pi_s + 2\pi_s]$ reaction. (B) True: Azide + alkyne (Huisgen cycloaddition) forms a 1,2,3-triazole. (C) True: Nitrone + alkene forms a 5-membered isoxazolidine. (D) False: Because the cycloaddition is concerted and suprafacial, it is strictly **stereospecific** (*cis*-alkenes give *cis*-substituted adducts). Hence, (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Reaction of $4.00\text{ g}$ of cyclohexa-1,3-diene (molar mass $= 80\text{ g mol}^{-1}$) with excess maleic anhydride (molar mass $= 98\text{ g mol}^{-1}$) affords the $[4+2]$ Diels-Alder adduct in $85\%$ isolated yield. The mass of the adduct obtained (in $\text{g}$) is _____ (rounded off to two decimal places).
questions.explanationEn: Moles of limiting reagent cyclohexa-1,3-diene $= 4.00 / 80 = 0.050\text{ mol}$. Since the Diels-Alder reaction is a $1:1$ addition, the molar mass of the adduct is $80 + 98 = 178\text{ g mol}^{-1}$. At $85\%$ yield, moles of adduct $= 0.050 \times 0.85 = 0.0425\text{ mol}$, giving a mass of $0.0425 \times 178 = 7.565\text{ g} \approx 7.57\text{ g}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The number of newly created tetrahedral stereocenters ($sp^3$ chiral carbons) in the $[4+2]$ Diels-Alder adduct of $(2E,4E)$-hexa-2,4-diene with maleic anhydride is _____ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: In the $[4+2]$ cycloaddition between $(2E,4E)$-hexa-2,4-diene and maleic anhydride, both terminal carbons of the diene (bearing $-\text{CH}_3$ and $-\text{H}$) and both alkene carbons of maleic anhydride (bearing $-\text{C}(=\text{O})\text{O}-$ and $-\text{H}$) rehybridize from $sp^2$ to $sp^3$, each becoming bonded to four different substituents. Thus, $4$ new stereocenters are created simultaneously.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A three-step linear synthesis of an advanced pharmaceutical intermediate proceeds with individual step yields of $80\%$, $75\%$, and $90\%$, respectively. The overall percentage yield of the three-step sequence is _____ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: For a linear multi-step synthesis, the overall fractional yield is the product of the individual step fractional yields: $Y_{\text{overall}} = 0.80 \times 0.75 \times 0.90 = 0.54$, which corresponds to an overall yield of $54\%$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn:
The major product formed in the following three-step reaction sequence is:
Ethyl 4-oxopentanoate $\xrightarrow{\text{1. HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH, cat. } p\text{-TsOH};\; \text{2. DIBAL-H (1.0 equiv), toluene, }-78\,^\circ\text{C};\; \text{3. aq. H}_3\text{O}^+}$ ?
questions.explanationEn: Step 1 selectively protects the ketone of ethyl 4-oxopentanoate as a cyclic 1,3-dioxolane ketal while leaving the ester unaffected. Step 2 uses $1.0\text{ equiv}$ of $\text{DIBAL-H}$ at $-78\,^\circ\text{C}$ to reduce the ester selectively to an aldehyde (stopping at a stable aluminum hemiacetal at low temperature). Step 3 (aqueous acid workup) releases the aldehyde and removes the ketal protecting group, affording 4-oxopentanal.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Treatment of $(S)$-octan-2-ol with $\text{Ph}_3\text{P}$, diisopropyl azodicarboxylate (DIAD), and 4-nitrobenzoic acid in THF, followed by hydrolysis of the resulting ester with $\text{NaOH}/\text{MeOH}$, gives:
questions.explanationEn: The Mitsunobu reaction converts $(S)$-octan-2-ol into its 4-nitrobenzoate ester via $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ displacement of the oxyphosphonium intermediate ($\text{R}-\text{OP}^+\text{Ph}_3$) by 4-nitrobenzoate, proceeding with complete **inversion of configuration** to give $(R)$-octan-2-yl 4-nitrobenzoate. Subsequent alkaline saponification cleaves the acyl–oxygen bond without disturbing the C2 stereocenter, yielding **$(R)$-octan-2-ol**.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Treatment of $(R)$-2-methylcyclohexan-1-one with $\text{LDA}$ ($1.05\text{ equiv}$) in THF at $-78\,^\circ\text{C}$ followed by $\text{Me}_3\text{SiCl}$ gives silyl enol ether **X**; whereas treatment with $\text{Et}_3\text{N}$ and $\text{Me}_3\text{SiCl}$ in DMF at $130\,^\circ\text{C}$ gives silyl enol ether **Y**. Compounds **X** and **Y** are, respectively:
questions.explanationEn: A strong, sterically hindered base ($\text{LDA}$) at $-78\,^\circ\text{C}$ in aprotic THF performs **kinetic deprotonation** at the less hindered C6 methylene carbon to give the less substituted silyl enol ether **X**. Conversely, a weak reversible base ($\text{Et}_3\text{N}$) at high temperature ($130\,^\circ\text{C}$) allows equilibration to the **thermodynamic** (more substituted, tetrasubstituted) silyl enol ether **Y**.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Thermal $[2+2]$ cycloaddition between diphenylketene ($\text{Ph}_2\text{C}=\text{C}=\text{O}$) and $(Z)$-but-2-ene proceeds concertedly and stereospecifically to yield *cis*-3,4-dimethyl-2,2-diphenylcyclobutan-1-one. According to the Woodward-Hoffmann rules, this thermal $[2+2]$ reaction is symmetry-allowed because it operates as:
optionsEn: A $[\pi 2_s + \pi 2_a]$ cycloaddition in which the alkene reacts suprafacially and the ketene reacts antarafacially via orthogonal approach
questions.explanationEn: Because the linear $sp$-hybridized carbonyl carbon of a ketene has two orthogonal $\pi$-systems ($\text{C}=\text{C}$ and $\text{C}=\text{O}$) and low steric hindrance, the alkene can approach orthogonally in a concerted $[\pi 2_s + \pi 2_a]$ geometry (alkene suprafacial, ketene antarafacial). This $4\pi$-electron thermal pathway is Woodward-Hoffmann allowed and strictly preserves the *cis* stereochemistry of $(Z)$-but-2-ene.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Upon UV irradiation ($h\nu$) in methanol, 2-methylcyclohexan-1-one undergoes Norrish Type I $\alpha$-cleavage selectively at the more substituted $\text{C}1-\text{C}2$ bond to form an acyl–alkyl 1,6-diradical. Subsequent intramolecular hydrogen-atom transfer to the acyl radical followed by trapping of the resulting ketene with $\text{MeOH}$ affords:
questions.explanationEn: Norrish Type I cleavage of 2-methylcyclohexan-1-one breaks the $\text{C}1-\text{C}2$ bond to form the secondary alkyl–acyl 1,6-diradical $\cdot\text{C}(=\text{O})(\text{CH}_2)_4\dot{\text{C}}\text{HCH}_3$. Note the two competing H-transfers: (1) H-transfer from C6 (adjacent to $\text{C}=\text{O}$) to the secondary alkyl radical C2 generates a **ketene**, $\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_4\text{CH}=\text{C}=\text{O}$, which is trapped by $\text{MeOH}$ to yield **methyl heptanoate**; (2) H-transfer from the C2-methyl/C3 to the acyl radical gives an unsaturated aldehyde (hept-5-enal). Thus, the ketene-trapped ester product is methyl heptanoate.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following rearrangements proceed with **retention of configuration** at the migrating chiral carbon center?
optionsEn: Baeyer-Villiger oxidation of an optically active ketone
Curtius rearrangement of an optically active acyl azide
Hofmann rearrangement of an optically active primary amide
Mitsunobu esterification of an optically active secondary alcohol
questions.explanationEn: The Baeyer-Villiger (A), Curtius (B), and Hofmann (C) rearrangements are all concerted intramolecular 1,2-migrations from carbon to an electron-deficient heteroatom (O or N) in which the migrating group attacks from the front face of its own bonding orbital, proceeding with complete **retention of configuration**. Mitsunobu esterification (D) is an intermolecular $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ reaction proceeding with *inversion*. Hence, (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following dienes are **unreactive** (or react extremely slowly) in a standard thermal Diels-Alder reaction with maleic anhydride?
questions.explanationEn: A concerted Diels-Alder reaction strictly requires the 1,3-diene to adopt the ***s-cis*** conformation. (A) $(2Z,4Z)$-Hexa-2,4-diene suffers severe steric clash between its two internal methyl groups in the *s-cis* conformation, making it virtually unreactive. (D) 3-Methylenecyclohex-1-ene is rigidly locked in an *s-trans* conformation and cannot undergo Diels-Alder cycloaddition. By contrast, 1,2-dimethylenecyclohexane (B) and cyclopenta-1,3-diene (C) are locked *s-cis* and are highly reactive. Hence, (A) and (D) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling of $18.70\text{ g}$ of 4-bromoanisole ($\text{C}_7\text{H}_7\text{BrO}$, molar mass $= 187\text{ g mol}^{-1}$) with excess phenylboronic acid ($\text{PhB(OH)}_2$) in the presence of $\text{Pd(PPh}_3)_4$ and aqueous $\text{K}_2\text{CO}_3$ produces the biaryl coupling product in $88\%$ isolated yield. The mass of the biaryl product obtained (in $\text{g}$) is _____ (rounded off to two decimal places). [Given: atomic masses: $\text{H} = 1$, $\text{C} = 12$, $\text{O} = 16$]
questions.explanationEn: Moles of limiting reagent 4-bromoanisole $= 18.70 / 187 = 0.100\text{ mol}$. Suzuki-Miyaura coupling yields 4-methoxybiphenyl ($\text{C}_{13}\text{H}_{12}\text{O}$), whose molar mass is $13(12) + 12(1) + 16 = 184\text{ g mol}^{-1}$. At $88\%$ yield, moles of product $= 0.100 \times 0.88 = 0.088\text{ mol}$, giving a mass of $0.088 \times 184 = 16.192\text{ g} \approx 16.19\text{ g}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Photochemical Paterno-Büchi $[2+2]$ cycloaddition between benzaldehyde ($\text{PhCHO}$) and furan yields exclusively the *exo*-oxetane adduct, 6-phenyl-2,7-dioxabicyclo[3.2.0]hept-3-ene. The number of tetrahedral stereocenters ($sp^3$ chiral carbon atoms) present in this bicyclic oxetane adduct is _____ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: In the Paterno-Büchi cycloaddition of benzaldehyde with one $\text{C}=\text{C}$ bond of furan, the carbonyl oxygen bonds to C2 of furan (generating the stabilized allylic radical at C3) and the benzaldehyde carbon bonds to C3 of furan. This converts three $sp^2$ carbons into $sp^3$ stereocenters: the acetal bridgehead C1 (attached to two oxygens, C5, and H), the allylic bridgehead C5 (attached to C1, C4, C6, and H), and the benzylic C6 (attached to O7, C5, Ph, and H). Thus, there are $3$ chiral carbon centers.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Synthesis, Reagents, Pericyclic & Photochemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Heating allyl 2,6-dimethylphenyl ether at $200\,^\circ\text{C}$ induces a cascade $[3,3]$-Claisen rearrangement followed by a $[3,3]$-Cope rearrangement and tautomerization to yield a single major aromatic product. The total number of $sp^2$-hybridized carbon atoms in this major product is _____ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: Because both *ortho* positions of allyl 2,6-dimethylphenyl ether are blocked by methyl groups, the initial *ortho*-Claisen intermediate (6-allyl-2,6-dimethylcyclohexa-2,4-dien-1-one) cannot tautomerize to a phenol. Instead, it undergoes a second $[3,3]$-sigmatropic (Cope) shift to C4 followed by tautomerization to yield **4-allyl-2,6-dimethylphenol** ($\text{C}_{11}\text{H}_{14}\text{O}$). Counting its $sp^2$-hybridized carbons: $6$ aromatic ring carbons $+\; 2$ vinylic carbons in the $-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$ allyl group $= 8$ $sp^2$ carbons.
